feedback.Physical Object: Excluded — The algorithm is abstract and has no tangible instantiation.
feedback.Synthetic: Included — Encryption algorithms are entirely human-designed.
feedback.Biological/Biomimetic: Excluded — Not modeled on biological systems.
feedback.Powered: Excluded — As an algorithmic form, it has no energy dependence.
feedback.Structural: Excluded — It has no physical structure.
feedback.Observable: Excluded — Only its representations are observable, not the algorithm itself.
feedback.Physical Medium: Excluded — It is symbolic and immaterial.
feedback.Active: Excluded — Requires a system to be activated; not independently active.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Included — Encryption algorithms are explicitly constructed for confidentiality and security.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Included — They deterministically produce ciphertext as output.
feedback.Processes Signals/Logic: Included — Operate entirely through logic and symbolic transformation.
feedback.State-Transforming: Included — Most encryption algorithms involve multi-step, internal state transitions across rounds.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Excluded — Typically interfaced through systems, not designed for direct human interaction.
feedback.System-integrated: Included — Embedded within security protocols, systems, and digital infrastructure.
feedback.Functionally Autonomous: Excluded — Cannot operate independently of a computational system.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — Critical in many systems, but not universally essential across domains.
feedback.Symbolic: Included — Defined in terms of symbolic logic and formal notation.
feedback.Signalling: Included — Alters and encodes the information structure of data.
feedback.Rule-governed: Included — Adheres strictly to formal, stepwise rules.
feedback.Compositional: Included — Built from modular components (e.g., rounds, S-boxes, key expansion).
feedback.Normative: Included — Specifies exact transformations and expected outcomes.
feedback.Meta: Included — Can be reasoned about abstractly; often used in comparison or derivation of other algorithms.
feedback.Temporal: Included — Requires ordered, time-based steps (e.g., rounds, block sequences).
feedback.Digital/Virtual: Included — Exists entirely in the digital realm as an abstraction.
feedback.Social Construct: Included — The very idea of encryption is rooted in human-defined secrecy protocols.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Included — Standardized by NIST, NSA, ISO, and other organizations.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Excluded — Not tied to social or personal identity itself.
feedback.Regulated: Included — Historically treated as weapons; today subject to national and international export controls.
feedback.Economically Significant: Included — Encryption is foundational to finance, commerce, and cybersecurity.
feedback.Politicised: Included — Central to privacy, surveillance, and civil liberties debates; targeted by state policies.
feedback.Ritualised: Excluded — Used procedurally but not embedded in symbolic cultural rituals.
feedback.Ethically Significant: Included — Directly implicated in ethical concerns around privacy, freedom, and harm.

encoding_notes: This encoding treats the encryption algorithm not just as a symbolic or logical entity, but as a deeply consequential abstraction. It transforms state, produces real effects, and sits at the intersection of technological systems and social, political, and ethical structures. The inclusion of multiple social traits reflects its active role in shaping digital life and global governance.
